correctness.rationale: For every escaping orbit of \(Q_{\pm1}\), odd returns are \(y_{i+1}=k_iy_i\) with \(k_i=(y_i\pm1)/2^{v_2(y_i\pm1)}\ge3\). Since \(\gcd(k_i,y_i)=1\), every return introduces a new odd prime. Then \(y_r\ge(r+2)!/2\) and \(r\le(1+o(1))\log y_r/\log\log y_r\). An ordinary-time block has at most \((r+1)\log_2(y_r+1)\) steps and all its states are at least \(y_r\), yielding \(\liminf\log x_t/\sqrt{t\log t}\ge\sqrt{\log2/2}\). All boundary cases, quantifiers, initial even segments, and the logarithm base are handled in RESULT.md. The self-contained exact-arithmetic program passed 2157 return, 947 coprimality, and 947 prime-bound checks; the asymptotic proof does not rely on computations.

value.rationale: The Oct 2026 classification of bounded orbits leaves quantitative escape speed unspecified. Each escaping odd return has at least one genuinely new prime divisor, a nontrivial arithmetical persistence law, and this translates into an explicit stretched-exponential floor for the actual number of steps, even with arbitrarily long halvings. The combination of prime-support growth with full-clock control makes a natural structurally motivated refinement, rather than a finite verification or minor parameter change. The bound does not require claiming sharpness.
